RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the August 5, 2005/Sravana 14, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Amendment of Indian Forest
Act, 1927
*181. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of  ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering  to amend the Indian Forest
Act, 1927;
(b) if so, whether Government have
also decided to pass the Scheduled
Tribes (Recognition of Forest Rights)
Bill;
(c) whether the Forest Conservation
Act, 1980 which expanded IFA's scope by
centralizing State powers over forests made
the prior approval of the Central
Government necessary for dereservation
of reserved forests for use of forest land
for non-forest purposes; and
(d) by what time the Bill is likely to be
introduced and passed?
Anthrax disease
*182. SHRI N.K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any State in the country is
under Anthrax threat and if so, the details
of cases of Anthrax disease reported so far,
State-wise;
(b) the precautions proposed to be
taken by Government to check the disease;
and
(c) whether any package of assistance
has been made available to the State
Governments under the Centrally
sponsored schemes to control the disease?
Wheat production
†*183. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the stock of
wheat during July, 2005 in the country has
come down to around 143 lakh tonnes;

56
(b) if so, the reasons for continuous
decline in the production of wheat;
(c) the steps being taken by
Government for increasing production of
wheat to keep pace with the increase in
population of the country;
(d) the scheme formulated by
Government to increase wheat production
and various other crops so that their
production does not decline in future;
and
(e) whether Government would also ban
residential use of agricultural land to
increase the production of wheat and
various other crops, if not, the reasons
therefor?
Expansion of RINL
*184. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS
KAUR:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Planning
Commission has approved the expansion
plan for Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL)
to increase its production from the present
31/2 million tonnes to 7 million tonnes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government are seriously thinking of
merging RINL with SAIL;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether any consultations with
State Government and the major political
parties of the State have been held; and
(f) if so, what are Government's views
thereon?
Impact of Patent Laws on pharma
sector
*185. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have assessed
the impact of recent Patent Laws on the
restructuring of pharma-sector in the
country;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) if so, whether such restructuring
would cause the closure of some units;
(d) if so, what will be the extent of
unemployment due to closure of units; and
(e) what steps are being taken to absorb
the skilled manpower of the closed units?
Streamlining Healthcare system
*186. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether, in a bid to streamline and
step up healthcare system in the country,
Planning Commission has suggested
measures including setting up a Public
Health Development Authority with a
corpus of Rs. 500 crore and launching
'Sarwa Swasthya Abhiyan' to make
healthcare accessible to all;
(b) if so, whether any concrete measures
have been suggested by them as to how
these healthcare schemes have to be
implemented; and
(c) if so, by when Government are likely
to implement such schemes?

57
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Rent paid to private godowns
by FCI
*187. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS,  FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the rent paid to private godowns by
the Food Corporation of India in 2004-05
in the country;
(b) the rent expected to be paid by FCI
to private godowns in 2005-06 in the
country;
(c) whether it is a fact that FCI had
entered into agreements with a number of
private godown owners during the last three
years;
(d) whether it is also a fact that no  effort
has been made by FCI to review and ask
the godown owners to reduce their rents
and charges; and
(e) the reasons for this soft approach
towards godown owners who are
profiteering on

List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions —155
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Animal diseases in U.P.
†1264. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration for Central
assistance to check animal diseases in Uttar
Pradesh; and
(b) if so, the reasons for delay in its
implementation and the details of the
proposals received from Uttar Pradesh
Government for financial assistance?
Assistance to Karnataka for control of
pests and diseases
1265. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Karnataka
has sent any proposal for financial
assistance for control of pests and diseases
and rejuvenation of coconut palm in
Turuvekere Taluk of Tumkur District;
(b) if so, whether any assistance from
Central Development Board has been given
to Karnataka; and
(c) if not, by when the amount would
be released?
Crop damage due to floods
1266. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
assessment of extent of damage to the crops
due to recent floods in the various parts of
the country;
(b) if so, the details in terms of value of
the damaged crops and the area affected,
State-wise;
(c) the manner in which Government
plan to help the affected farmers;
(d) the details of the mechanism for
disbursing the help;
(e) whether Government have a
mechanism to monitor the actual disbursal
of help; and

289
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
MIS expenditure
1267. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state the total amount of money
spent on Market Invention Schemes and
market support operations during the years
2002-2003 to 2004-2005, commodity-wise
and year-wise?
Declining livestock
†1268. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the total livestock available in the
country at present;
(b) whether it is a fact that the number
of livestock has been declining for the last
five years in the country;
(c) whether Government are aware of
the involvement of slaughter houses in
slaughtering of  bovine, slaughtering of more
than authorised number of animals as also
the slaughtering of stolen animals; and
(d) the action being taken by
Government with regard to aforementioned
slaughter houses and particularly against
those situated in District Aligarh of Uttar
Pradesh?
ICAR research benefits to farmers
1269. SHRI B. K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the laboratories under the
ICAR have a dismal record of translating
their research/development efforts into real
on-field inputs for the farmers;
(b) whether the ICAR labs have brought
out nearly fourteen new high yielding
varieties of seeds but these have not at all
reached the farmers;
(c) whether the farmers are now relying
more on private sector for their hybrid seed
requirements; and
(d) the reasons for ICAR system, with
huge manpower and infrastructure, failing
to transfer its technology to the farmers?
Agricultural growth
†1270. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that agricultural
growth rate has come down to 1.5 per cent
from its desired target of 4 per cent during
the last three years since the beginning of
the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) whether it is a fact that necessary
and required investment has been
constantly decreasing in agricultural sector
since 1980 alongwith critical decrease in
agricultural research; and
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government
to bring desired improvement in agricultural
sector?
Policy for doubling agricultural
production
1271. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
declining trend in the growth rate of
agriculture and the performance of
agriculture has been disturbing;

†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) whether in such a situation, there is
a policy initiated to double our agricultural
production in ten years; and
(c) if so, the thrust and focus to achieve
this policy initiative in terms of investment
in the entire chain of agricultural activities,
infrastructural development, expansion and
upgradation?
